decisionMemo.businessProblem: A Series A SaaS company growing ARR 40% has support costs growing 60%, so support cost per customer and as a % of revenue are rising - operating leverage is inverting. Leadership treats this as the normal cost of scaling and plans to keep hiring support. Competing hypotheses: (1) it is benign scaling and adding support headcount is the right response; (2) tickets-per-customer is rising (1.6 -> 2.4), NRR slipped (108% -> 101%), and a growing share of tickets reportedly relate to confusion around two recently shipped features and onboarding - pointing to a product-friction / fit problem where adding support treats the symptom while the root cause (usability/defects/onboarding) drives both rising tickets and contraction; (3) a transient onboarding spike from a recent self-serve funnel change that will subside. Tickets have not been categorized by root cause or cohort, so the driver is not yet established.
